metadata.scenario_title: DUI Vehicular Manslaughter — State v. Marcus Webb

agents.reason: Although the BAC readings and the fact of the victim's death are established, I am not convinced beyond a reasonable doubt that the prosecution proved the statutory culpability and legal (proximate) causation required for conviction. The jury instructions leave open whether mere intoxication satisfies the culpability element and whether the defendant's conduct, as a matter of legal causation, was proved to the necessary degree; on those dispositive legal points reasonable doubt remains, so I must vote not_guilty.

agents.reason: After careful application of the court's instructions and the beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard to each element, I find the prosecution has not carried its burden on the statutory culpability and legal causation requirements. While the BAC and the tragic outcome are serious facts, intoxication alone as presented does not, under the instructions we were given, remove reasonable doubt about the requisite mental state, nor does the record establish proximate causation to the extent the law demands. The burden rests entirely with the State, and that burden has not been satisfied beyond a reasonable doubt.
